title: Beta-to-scale surge simulation & roleplay cue-sheet
body:
Purpose:
This is a working cue-sheet for the beta->scale surge simulation exercise. Goal: validate staffflow, gating thresholds, and KPI degradation tolerances before we open the first 10k users to the hosted API. Document is intentionally lightweight — use for roleplay rehearsals and for creating concise runbook tasks we can hand to oncall and product leads.

Scope and constraints:
- Feature set: hosted API text-gen v2 (no tool-calls) + embeddings for search.
- Target region: us-west1.
- Environment: dedicated staging cluster that mirrors production quantization profile.
- Duration for each scenario: 30–90m active traffic window, 2h follow-up observation.
- This is not a security or compliance test (we have separate checklist).

Primary simulation objectives:
1) Staffflow validation: ensure role handoffs happen within SLA (max 5m alert-to-ack for SRE lead during high-severity throttles).
2) KPI observation: capture token-level cost vs latency tradeoffs and detect when quality alerts spike.
3) Gating and rollback: validate automated throttle and slow-roll decisions triggered by objective thresholds.
4) Communications: run a roleplay for external comms + Cx escalation.

Success KPIs (baseline / tolerance / abort):
- P50 latency (text gen): baseline 120ms / acceptable +40% / abort if >300ms sustained 5m
- P95 latency: baseline 420ms / acceptable +50% / abort if >900ms sustained 5m
- Errors (5xx + model errors): baseline 0.2% / acceptable up to 1.0% / abort at >2.5% sustained 3m
- Token cost per 1k tokens: baseline $0.18 / monitor for +30% deviation (investigate)
- Quality regressions (eval set auto-check): baseline 95% pass / abort if <85% on critical prompt set
- Throughput achieved: verify we can sustain a 3x beta traffic spike without breaching latency abort thresholds

Scenarios (run in order, stop when abort condition hit):
A — Warm surge (smoke): 3x beta traffic for 30m, steady ramp-up 10m -> hold 20m. Purpose: sanity-check autoscale and work-queue behavior.
B — Spike + KV-cache churn: sudden 10x spike for 5m (simulate many new sessions causing KV cache misses), then decay to 2x for 25m. Purpose: validate cache warming behavior and eviction policy.
C — Sustained heavy (stress): 2.5x sustained for 90m while injecting 5% malformed requests and 1% high-cost prompts (long context). Purpose: check long-tail latency and cost burn.

Roleplay cue-sheet (role -> actions with minute offsets relative to scenario start):
- Product Ops Lead (Laura): T-10m: confirm comms channel (Zoom + #beta-launch). T+0: announce start, publish expected KPIs. T+5: check initial telemetry and call SRE if P95 > 600ms. T+15: summarize and note action items.
- SRE Lead (Sanjay): T-0: validate rollout knobs (throttles, model fallbacks) are set to default. T+2: confirm autoscale events in infra console. T+6: if P95 > 700ms, execute tiered throttle 1 (10% reject). T+10: escalate to infra if errors spike.
- Serving Runtime Engineer (Evan): T-3: standby on-call terminal, watch GPU saturation, KV hit rate. T+4: if cache miss rate > 40%, trigger cache pre-warm job. T+8: if P50 increases >50% and GPU util < 80%, investigate scheduler.
- Customer Success (Marisa): T+0: prepare templated messages for beta customers. T+12: roleplay inbound ticket triage and log any customer-impacting examples.
- Comms / Legal (Tomás): T+0: confirm embargo and escalation path. T+30: approve any external notices if an outage occurs.

Staffing run-rate (quick reference):
- SRE: 2 engineers (lead + backup) during simulation window
- Serving runtime: 1 engineer (hot standby)
- Product ops: 1 lead + 1 coordinator
- CS/Support: 2 agents on rotation
- Infra (autoscale/capacity): 1 engineer monitor
- Observability: 1 engineer to patch dashboards and ensure ingestion

Gating thresholds & automated triggers (what the system should do):
- Auto-throttle: if error rate >1.5% OR P95 > 750ms, trigger tier-1 throttle (10% reject) for 2m, then re-evaluate.
- Model fallback: if quality eval drops below 90% for 2 consecutive buckets (5m each), route new requests to model v1-compat (lower throughput) while preserving correctness.
- Regional fallback: if us-west1 CPU/RAM pressure > 85% for 10m, route 30% traffic to us-west2 regional replica.

Monitoring signals to record (dashboard names / panel ids):
- API: text-gen latency p50/p95/p99 (panel: api-textgen-latency)
- Runtime: GPU util / mem / KV hit rate (panel: runtime-gpu-kv)
- Cost: token_cost_per_request (panel: cost-token-1k)
- Quality: eval-pass-rate / hallucination-rate on test prompts (panel: eval-quality)
- Errors: 4xx / 5xx / model-exception (panel: api-errors)

Fallback & graceful degradation playbook (short):
1) Tiered throttle -> protect SLOs.
2) Model fallback to smaller quantized variant if cost/latency spike.
3) Disable non-critical features (e.g., long-context parsing) if under sustained load.
4) Open support banner to customers and follow comms template.

Rehearsal schedule (proposed):
- Fri 2025-01-24 14:00–17:00: dry-run (no external monitoring).
- Mon 2025-01-27 09:00–12:00: full run with CS roleplay and sample customers.
- Wed 2025-01-29 13:00–17:00: focused cache-churn scenario.

Postmortem template (to complete within 48h):
- Summary of what happened (one paragraph).
- Timeline of key events (timeline with minute marks).
- KPIs recorded vs expected (include raw screenshots/links).
- Root cause and contributing factors.
- Action items (owner + due date).
- Follow-ups (capacity changes, infra optimizations, docs updates).

Open questions / TODOs (short list):
- TODO: Confirm us-west2 regional replica capacity for routing (assign: Tomás; due: 2025-01-15).
- Q: Do we want the automated throttle to progressively increase rejects or always a fixed 10%? (decide in run debrief).
- TODO: Add the evaluation prompt set into the CI job that runs during simulation (assign: Evan; due: 2025-01-20).
- Q: How should billing alerts be handled for sudden token cost spikes (hook to finance)? (action: Sanjay to loop in finance).

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally operational and a bit terse. Use it as the quick cue for roleplay; expand into a full runbook after two dry-runs.
- If you edit thresholds, add a brief rationale and past-run references in the linked Confluence page.

Change log:
- 2025-01-10 (Laura): initial draft with scenario skeleton.
- 2025-01-15 (Sanjay): added gating thresholds and staffing run-rate.
- 2025-01-22 (Evan): updated cache-churn scenario and monitoring panel ids.
notes: Informal working doc: contains roleplay steps and candidate thresholds. Finalize after 2 rehearsals and include concrete dashboard links in Confluence.
